title: Compare Linked Lists of Strings
statement:
You are given two singly linked lists whose nodes each hold a **non-empty string chunk**. Reading a list from head to tail and joining its chunks in order gives the string that the list represents.

Determine whether the two lists represent the **same string**. Chunk boundaries do not have to match: the lists `["ab", "c"]` and `["a", "bc"]` both represent `abc`, so they are equal.

Print `true` if the two represented strings are identical and `false` otherwise.

The lists can be long, so a good solution walks both lists at the same time with two pointers (a node pointer and a character offset inside the current chunk) instead of building the two full strings first.
inputFormat: The first line contains `n`, the number of nodes in the first list. The second line contains `n` space-separated strings (the chunks, head to tail). The third line contains `m`, the number of nodes in the second list. The fourth line contains `m` space-separated strings.
constraints: Every chunk is a non-empty string of lowercase letters
The total number of characters in each list is at most 5 · 10^5

examples.explanation: Both lists spell `abcdef`, although the chunks are split differently.
The first list spells `hellowor` and the second `helloworld`. The first is a proper prefix of the second, so the strings differ.
The lists have the same length but spell `xyz` and `xya`, which differ in the last character.

hints: Walking character by character is enough: you never need the whole string in memory.
Keep for each list a pair (current node, index inside the current chunk). Compare the two current characters and advance both.
When a pointer reaches the end of its chunk, move to the next node. The lists are equal only if both run out at exactly the same moment with no mismatch before.
